# AbstractEntity

AbstractEntity is the entity app of [AbstractFramework](https://github.com/lpalbou):
the place where you create entities, talk with them, watch what they remember as a
live memory graph, and read their diaries. It is published on npm as
`@abstractframework/entity` and runs as a small local web app in front of your
[AbstractGateway](https://github.com/lpalbou/AbstractGateway).

## What's new

0.12.0 follows the entity's five-state life cycle: the phase bar shows **idle**, **visit**,
**work**, **personal** and **sleep**; own time is the one toggle you grant, work is the jobs
queued for him, the red **Stop** halts everything and cancels his own time, and **Resume** brings
him back idle. **Settings → Mind → Sleep** sets when an idle entity sleeps for maintenance. In a
conversation, type `@` to bring other entities in; each answers once, under its own name. Under
a reply, badges show what the turn kept (a diary entry, a lesson, an interest, a question, a
realization), and while he answers, the chat shows what he is doing, step by step. The memory
graph is laid out by the topics his memory forms in his sleep, with a grey-to-green usage scale and
the paths he travelled to each recalled memory. The **Topics** panel opens at the top right, and
you can move and resize it; each topic is a card in its colour, with its memory types and the paths
he travelled most. A legend you can click shows where each kind of memory or link sits, and
**Monitor** beside **Live** in the timeline opens the Cognitive Monitor under the graph. All of
this needs AbstractGateway 0.21.0. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md#0120---2026-11-10) and
[Reading the memory graph](#reading-the-memory-graph).

0.11.2 shows every entity on the home page at once: each tile appears as soon as the
list arrives and fills in on its own, and a slow entity no longer holds the others on
"reading his card…". **Settings → identity** is now one clear page from the shared kit:
the look, then the voice (choosing a voice plays a short sample; **Create a new voice**
when none fits), the history, and one **Save** at the bottom. See the
[changelog](CHANGELOG.md#0112---2026-11-07).

0.11.1 keeps the cognitive readings attached to the reply on screen: the emotional
diagram shows that reply's measurements even when you move between replies while they
load. In the Avatar view the avatar speaks only while you can hear it, the live line
and the answer each have their own read-aloud button, and completed answers no longer
carry an accent border. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md#0111---2026-11-07).

0.11.0 gives each entity its own identity and a track record. **Settings → identity**
keeps its look (design and colour) and its voice in one record that you save once and
the gateway checks; the Avatar view draws the entity in that design and colour.
**Settings → track record** counts its sessions, runs, successes, failures and tokens,
shows its trust for each kind of task as a completion rate only (a success means the
task finished; nobody has judged the quality of the work yet), and lists **who it has
met**: the people and the other entities, how many times, first and last. The
**Avatar** view also gets one live line under the avatar (click it for **Reply to
this** or **Latest**) and a **Findings** panel that collects what the entity
established (a sheet on a phone). All of this needs AbstractGateway 0.20.0 or newer.
See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md#0110---2026-11-04).

0.10.0 adds an optional **Avatar** conversation view (public subtitles, questions,
corrections and permission requests; needs AbstractGateway 0.19.0 or newer), the
shared rounded composer in the chat drawer and the meet console, and the shared
account widget in the top bar. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md#0100---2026-11-02).

## What is an entity?

An entity is an AI companion with a lasting memory of its own. You give it a
name; from then on it remembers what you talk about, keeps a diary, sleeps to
sort its memories and grows over time. It lives on your AbstractGateway (its
memory is stored there, in its own folder), and it keeps one identity for its
whole life. In this app you can talk with it, watch what it remembers as a
live graph, and read its diary.

An entity is always in one of five states: **idle** (awake, nothing to do),
**personal** (its own time, which only you grant), **work** (jobs queued for
it), **visit** (someone is talking with it) or **sleep** (maintenance of its
memory). Every interaction forms a memory. The red **Stop** halts everything at
once; **Resume** brings it back idle. See
[The entity life cycle](docs/entity-phases.md).

## Your first entity

1. Open the Entity app. From the gateway console, the Entity card's button
   reads **Create your first entity** while the gateway has none; it opens
   the app signed in, straight on the creation form. That console button
   needs AbstractGateway 0.4.1 or newer; the app itself works with any
   gateway.
2. Type a name (for example *Pollux*) and press **Create entity**. The name is
   all it needs: the entity starts from the standard starting document.
3. The app opens the new entity's page. Say hello in the **Chat** tab.

With no entity yet, the app shows **No entities yet**, one sentence on what an
entity is, and the same **Create your first entity** button. The address
`http://127.0.0.1:3007/#new` opens the creation form directly (the gateway
console uses it). The **Advanced: starting document** fold of the form takes
your own starting document (YAML) if you write one.

A name belongs to one entity for its whole life: creating an entity whose name
already exists opens the existing one instead.

## Install and run

AbstractEntity needs Node.js 18 or newer and an AbstractGateway to talk to.

```bash
# run without installing
npx @abstractframework/entity

# or install the `abstractentity` command globally
npm install -g @abstractframework/entity
abstractentity

# point it at your gateway (default: the gateway installed on this computer,
# else http://127.0.0.1:8080)
npx @abstractframework/entity --gateway-url http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

The app serves on `http://127.0.0.1:3007`. Open it and sign in to your gateway
from the connect dialog. When your gateway manages the Entity app (the gateway
console's **Apps** screen), open it from there instead: the gateway serves it
at `/apps/entity/` on its own address. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md)
for the full first run and [the configuration reference](docs/api.md#configuration)
for every launch flag.

## What you can do in the app

- **Entities list** (`/`): create entities, open one, watch them all at once
  (**watch all**) and convene two of them into one conversation (**convene a
  meet**). Each entity is a card with **Watch**, **Retry** when its own time
  stopped unexpectedly and **Resume** when it is stopped.
- **Entity page** (`/?entity=NAME`): the memory graph, the chat, and a set of
  reading tabs over the same life.

| Surface | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Phase bar | Where the entity is in its life cycle (idle, own time, work, visit, sleep or stopped), with a sentence, since when and where it goes next ("then: own time"); the **personal** toggle that grants its own time, **sleep now**, and the red **Stop** (or **Resume**). Beside it, one status line (the whole sentence on hover) and the **Files** (his home workspace, read-only) and **Settings** buttons. See [The entity life cycle](docs/entity-phases.md) |
| Memory graph | The entity's memories as a live graph, laid out by his topics (the groups his memory forms and titles in his sleep; with **topics** on, their circles, titles and the **Topics** panel), or as a force-directed graph until his topics are served (before his first sleep, or on an older gateway). Memories and lines run from grey (rarely used) to green (most used). After a reply, the **Context** view lights what he held in mind and the paths he travelled to each recalled memory. The toolbar holds **search**, **topics** and **Context**; the two-line legend under the graph names the kinds of memories and lines, and a click on one lights where they sit. With replay, time scrub and live tail. See [Reading the memory graph](#reading-the-memory-graph) |
| Chat | Visits: talk with the entity, see its reasoning cycles and tool use, adjust its mind (Gateway default or its own provider and model), its identity (avatar design, colour and voice, with their history), files, tools and system prompt in **Settings**, and read its track record (what it has done, trust by task, whom it has met) — an admin or the entity's creator changes them (gateway 0.14+: someone else reads its mind and identity with the gateway's sentence "Only an admin or <entity>'s creator can change its settings."). Replies can be read aloud in the entity's own voice (sentence by sentence, **Stop** any time) and the composer microphone dictates through the gateway's default speech-to-text route. In its **tools** tab each tool in each phase is a switch that applies at once and writes only that phase to `tool_policy.yaml`; a refused change switches back and shows the reason |
| Card | The entity's identity card: values, purposes, likes, open questions, interests, key moments and life so far |
| Detail | One memory: its verbatim text, feelings and associations |
| Book | The diary as a day-grouped journal; sealed entries stay sealed |
| Lessons | What the entity has learned and kept |
| World | The entity's short orientation cards about people, systems and ideas it has met |
| Health | Memory counts, recall coverage, sessions, model usage and on-disk footprint |
| Ledger | The continuous life ledger: memories formed, recalled, committed, appraised, diary and maintenance |
| Meet console | Two entities in one conversation: steer it, watch both sides, read it afterwards |
| Cognitive Monitor | Opened with **🧠 Monitor**, after **Live** in the timeline's controls, under the graph: the expressive character of the entity's own words (not its inner state), at the timeline's position while you replay (**read his words** scores them) and, live with the chat open, for the reply in view |

In a conversation, type `@` to bring another entity in: pick it from the list
of entities your account can see, and it becomes a chip inside your sentence (the
first pick says "Nerin will read this conversation's history"). When you send,
the entity you are talking with answers first, then each entity you picked, one
after the other in your order, so the second one reads the first one's answer.
Each answer shows who wrote it: the entity's avatar, its name and an "entity"
tag. An entity busy elsewhere is skipped with "Pollux is in another
conversation."; one that cannot answer puts your words and its chip back in the
message box. A gateway without mentions says "This gateway does not offer
mentions yet". See [Mentions in a conversation](docs/api.md#mentions-in-a-conversation).

Under a reply, a badge shows each thing the turn kept: a diary entry, a lesson, an
interest, a question or a realization, with its title (a private diary entry shows
no words). Click a badge to open its record.

Chat also offers an optional **Avatar** view. It brings the entity to the center
of the scene with one live line of what it reports, a Findings panel and the same composer,
files and voice controls. Chat remains the default. Switching views keeps the
current work and draft; the technical panels and their saved width return when
you switch back. The Avatar view needs AbstractGateway 0.19.0 or newer; with an
older gateway it cannot show progress messages (it asks you to begin a new
conversation, or says the public conversation could not be refreshed), and Chat
works as before. New Avatar visits request public updates, and Flow turns request
them when started in Avatar. An already running visit keeps its original settings.
Permission requests show ordinary actions and destinations, labeled decision icons,
and the assistant’s public reason when it is attached to that exact request. “Review
details” returns to the detailed Chat view. Unknown actions require that review.

While work runs, send a correction in the composer. The gateway may accept it
for the assistant's next opportunity; acceptance does not confirm that the plan
changed. If the entity asks a question, the same composer answers that exact
question. Permission requests keep separate Allow/Deny controls. Refused messages
stay in the composer for retry. Public updates keep their source IDs for the technical view, and diary fences
are screened before the live line, the findings or narration. The avatar shows activity and, under it, one live line: the latest thing the entity reports while it works, replaced as soon as something new arrives (nothing cycles). Click it to read it in full, then **Reply to this** to answer it or **Latest** to follow again. The findings it reports (facts or evidence it established) accumulate in a **Findings** panel beside the avatar, or a sheet you open with **Findings** on a phone; open one to see the results it came from. The answer appears once, as a message, with Markdown, links and files like the conversation. A question, a
permission request and a finished answer are each signalled with both a visual and
an audio cue; the view itself has no cue settings. Optional narration uses the
existing read-aloud setting and the entity's own voice. History, reconnects and hidden panels stay silent.
Reopening a visit restores its public conversation, including actual answers, expired
questions with their declared fallback, and late replies retained for their original
question. A fallback is a system outcome, not a human answer. This public view is bounded; when the gateway omits earlier
exchanges or descendant runs, it says **Some earlier exchanges are not shown in
this view.** The durable conversation remains on the gateway.

The app is a thin client: it keeps no server state of its own. Every view is
read from the gateway, and the memory views are computed from the memory
engine's replay stream, so replay, live tail and scrubbing back in time show the
same picture. See [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) for how this works.

Without a reachable gateway the app opens a bundled demo life, so you can
explore the memory graph offline.

The **About** button in the top bar shows the app's version, the AbstractFramework
and AbstractGateway versions your gateway reports, and the project links; see [the FAQ](docs/faq.md#how-do-i-see-which-versions-i-am-running).

### Reading the memory graph

Each dot is a memory. Its fill runs from dark grey (rarely used) to green (most used), ranked
within his own life, and the lines between memories follow the same scale for how often he used
the two together. Zoomed in, a small core shows the memory's kind, in the colours of the legend's
first line. An amber (orange) line is a pair he used together a moment ago; it fades as he goes
on.

After a reply, **Context** lights what he held in mind and rings each memory by why it came: gold
for the memories he always keeps in mind (present by right), pink for continuity (memories that
followed from the last ones) and blue for the memories found for this message (matched). A lit
line is the path he travelled to reach a recalled memory, in its ring's colour: pink for a trail
followed from the last memories, blue for this message's match. The links his memory names
(`continues`, `derived_from`, `mentions` and the others) are always faint grey, with a mark at the
end they point to (an arrow, a double chevron, a circle, a diamond, a square or a bar); the legend
lists them by name. The Context box over the graph says what each ring and the lit lines mean.

Click a kind or a link type in the legend to light where those memories sit and frame them; click
it again, or press Escape, to let go. Memories closed when a newer version replaced them, or when
they were retracted, stay hidden until you press the "◌ N closed memories" toggle after **fit**.

With **topics** on, each topic is a circle with its title, and the **Topics** panel lists them,
each a card in its circle's colour. On a wide graph the panel is docked at the top right: drag the
grip on its head to move it, its bottom-right corner to resize it, and **put back** to dock it
again; your browser remembers where you left it. Unfold a topic for what his memory knows of it:
its **Memory types** fold (rest on a type to light those memories, click it to list them) and its
paths most travelled (rest on a pair to light the two memories, click it to frame them).

## Responsive layout

The app works on a phone, a tablet, a resized browser window and a wide
monitor.

- **Desktop (1024 px and wider):** the side panel sits beside the memory graph.
  Drag its left edge to resize it; click the open tab to collapse it.
- **Tablet and narrow windows (below 1024 px):** the tab rail stays at the right
  edge and an open tab slides over the graph as a drawer. Close it with Escape,
  a tap outside it, or its close button. On a narrow screen the app opens with
  the panel closed, and a wider window brings back the panel you use on the
  desktop.
- **Phones (below 768 px, or held sideways):** the tabs become a strip along the
  bottom of the view, dialogs open from the bottom of the screen, and the header
  and timeline wrap onto a second row. Below 480 px the controls row swipes
  sideways, and the phase bar takes the first screen width: the five state
  words, **Stop**, then its sentence and any question on lines of their own.
- **On-screen keyboard:** while the keyboard is open, an open panel fills the
  screen above it with the tab strip kept underneath, so the chat stays usable.
- **Graph overlays:** when the graph is narrower than 860 px, the toolbar
  (search, topics, Context) and the legend become one scrollable row each, the
  layout buttons (freeze, settle, fit) show their symbols only, and the
  **Topics** panel stays in place: it sits under the Context box and opens as a
  sheet over the graph.
- **Cognitive Monitor:** on a phone the open monitor takes the graph's place;
  press **Monitor** again to get the graph back.
- **Full-width panels on phones:** below 768 px the chat transcript, the
  ledger, the health panel and the entity list are flat sections without card
  borders, with a thin line between items and text that starts at the screen
  gutter.
- **Folding lists:** below 1024 px, where the side panel is a drawer, each list
  in the Detail tab has a heading you tap to fold it. Lists start open, and the
  app remembers each fold in this browser.
- **Touch screens:** buttons, selects and fields are at least 44 px tall, text
  fields use 16 px text, no text is smaller than 14 px, and the chat
  transcript reads at 15 px.
- **Text on a desktop:** text is at least 13 px, and the ledger and the tool
  grants at least 12 px. The graph's node labels keep their own sizes.

Limits:

- On a small phone (375 x 667) the memory graph gets about 275 px of height
  with the panel closed, because the header, phase controls, tab strip and
  timeline stay on screen. Larger phones give it more room.
- On a phone held sideways, an open panel covers the graph and the header; the
  tab strip stays visible under it.
- The side tabs are buttons: they do not support arrow-key navigation between
  tabs.

## Known limits

- A **Stop** that lands while the entity is in the middle of a model call can
  let that one call finish before everything halts; nothing new starts after
  it.
- A **mention** opens a visit with the mentioned entity for that conversation;
  the visit closes after 5 minutes without a new mention.

The full list is in [The entity life cycle](docs/entity-phases.md#known-limits).

## Sign-in and security

The `abstractentity` server includes the shared AbstractFramework sign-in proxy:
you sign in once with a gateway token, the server keeps the gateway session in
HttpOnly cookies, and the browser never stores the token. The server binds to
loopback (`127.0.0.1`) by default. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Develop from a checkout

```bash
npm install          # includes the shared UI packages (ui-kit, panel-chat)
npm run build
npm start            # serves dist/ on http://127.0.0.1:3007

npm run dev          # Vite dev server on :3007 with the same sign-in proxy
npm test             # vitest
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Getting started

This guide takes you from nothing to talking with your first entity. For what an
entity is, see [What is an entity?](../README.md#what-is-an-entity) in the README.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer.
- A running [AbstractGateway](https://github.com/lpalbou/AbstractGateway) and a
  gateway token to sign in with. The gateway console's **Create your first
  entity** shortcut needs AbstractGateway 0.4.1 or newer; the app itself works
  with any gateway.

## 1. Start the app

```bash
npx @abstractframework/entity
```

or install the command once:

```bash
npm install -g @abstractframework/entity
abstractentity
```

The app serves on `http://127.0.0.1:3007` and talks to the gateway installed on
this computer (else `http://127.0.0.1:8080`). If your gateway is elsewhere,
pass `--gateway-url`:

```bash
npx @abstractframework/entity --gateway-url http://192.168.1.20:8080
```

Every setting is listed in [API and configuration](api.md#configuration).

## 2. Sign in

Open `http://127.0.0.1:3007`. The connect dialog asks for your gateway token.
The server keeps your gateway session in HttpOnly cookies, so you sign in once
per browser and the token never sits in the page.

If you arrive from the gateway console, you are already signed in.

## 3. Create your first entity

With no entity yet, the app shows **No entities yet** and a **Create your first
entity** button. (From the gateway console, the Entity card's **Create your
first entity** button opens the same form; `http://127.0.0.1:3007/#new` does
too.)

1. Type a **Name**, for example *Pollux*.
2. Press **Create entity**. The button reads **Creating…** while the gateway
   sets the entity up, then the form reports **Pollux is ready.**
3. The app opens Pollux's page.

The name is all the entity needs: it starts from the standard starting
document. An entity keeps one identity for life, so if the name already exists
the form reports **Pollux already exists — opening it.** and opens that entity.

**Advanced: starting document** lets you paste your own starting document
(YAML). By default the gateway checks it against the framework rules; the
**Framework check** switch in the same fold turns that check off.

## 4. Talk with it

On the entity's page, open the **Chat** tab and say hello. Choose **Avatar** for
a focused conversation scene: one live line of what the entity reports, and the findings it has established so far; **Chat** keeps the transcript
and technical view. The draft and ongoing work survive view changes. New Avatar
visits request public updates; Flow turns request them when started in Avatar.
During work, send a correction in the same composer or answer the question shown.
An accepted correction is available to the assistant, but is not confirmation
that its plan changed. Questions and permission decisions stay separate.

A visit starts when you choose **visit** in the phase bar at the top of the
page. It opens in every state except stopped: when the entity is finishing a
step of its own, "waiting" shows beside **visit** until it is ready, and a
sleeping entity pauses its sleep for you and goes back to it when the visit
ends. Send a message in the composer to begin talking. In Chat, the memory graph
shows memories forming and being recalled, and the **Book** tab collects the
diary entries the entity writes.

Voice works in a visit when the gateway has voice installed (AbstractGateway
0.13.0 or later): the speaker on a
reply reads it aloud in the entity's own voice, and the microphone beside the
composer dictates (hold it while you speak, or tap to start and tap again to
stop). **Settings → identity** sets the entity's look (its avatar's design and
colour) and its voice, saved together; **Settings → voice** sets your own
speaker, microphone (with a Test and a level meter), spoken language and
**Read aloud**. **Settings → track record** shows what the entity has done, how
far it can be trusted for each kind of task, and whom it has met
(AbstractGateway 0.20.0 or later).

## 5. Bring another entity in

While you talk with one entity, type `@` in the message box and pick another
entity from the list (the first pick says "Nerin will read this conversation's
history"). When you send, the entity you are talking with answers first, then
each entity you picked, in your order; each answer shows the entity's avatar,
its name and an "entity" tag. If one is busy in another conversation, the app
says so and goes on with the next.

## 6. Its own time, sleep and Stop

A new entity starts **idle**: awake and visitable, with nothing of its own
running. Press the **personal** toggle in the phase bar to grant it its own
time: it then explores its own ideas, sleeps for maintenance when it needs to
and wakes by itself. Press it again to take its own time back; the entity
stays awake. While it is idle, once 24 hours have passed since its last sleep,
it has formed 500 new memories since then, or more than 15 % of its memories
are not yet settled, it goes to sleep for maintenance on its own; change these
thresholds in **Settings → Mind → Sleep**.

The red **Stop** asks first, then halts everything at once and cancels its own
time. **Resume** brings it back idle. Granting own time, Stop and Resume need
an admin account. See [The entity life cycle](entity-phases.md) for every
state and how to read the bar.

## Next steps

- Tour the tabs described in the [README](../README.md#what-you-can-do-in-the-app),
  and learn to read the graph's colours in
  [Reading the memory graph](../README.md#reading-the-memory-graph).
- On a phone or tablet, see how the layout adapts in
  [Responsive layout](../README.md#responsive-layout).
- Open **convene a meet** on the entities list to put two entities in one
  conversation.
- Read [Architecture](architecture.md) to see how the app reads a life from the
  gateway.
- Something not working? See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).


<!-- ============================================================ -->
<!-- SOURCE: docs/architecture.md -->
<!-- ============================================================ -->

# Architecture

AbstractEntity is a static React single-page app plus a small Node server
(`bin/cli.js`). The server hosts the built app and the shared AbstractFramework
sign-in proxy (`@abstractframework/app-server`, `appId: "abstractentity"`). The
app keeps no server state of its own: everything it shows comes from
AbstractGateway's entity routes and from the memory engine's replay stream.

Read [Getting started](getting-started.md) first if you have not run the app yet.
The full list of routes and settings is in [API and configuration](api.md); how
data moves through each surface is in [Data flow](DataFlow.md).

## Components and connections

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Browser
    SPA["Entity app (React SPA)<br/>entities list · entity page"]
  end
  subgraph Server["abstractentity server (bin/cli.js, :3007)"]
    Static["Static files from dist/<br/>SPA fallback"]
    Proxy["Sign-in proxy<br/>POST /api/connection/gateway<br/>HttpOnly session cookies"]
    Host["GET /app/host<br/>LAN address for entity handles"]
  end
  subgraph Gateway["AbstractGateway (:8080)"]
    Entities["/api/gateway/entities/*<br/>list · create · replay · life_state · lifecycle · communities<br/>chat · visits · summon · voice/tts/stream<br/>visit/{run}: state · guidance · answer · decision (Avatar)"]
    Sessions["/api/gateway/sessions/{id}/mentions<br/>@ mentions"]
    Meets["/api/gateway/entities/meets/*"]
    Embed["/api/gateway/embeddings"]
    Docs["/api/gateway/docs/corpus"]
    About["/api/gateway/about<br/>versions for the About dialog"]
    Voice["/api/gateway/voice/defaults · voice/voices<br/>attachments/upload · runs/{run}/audio/transcribe"]
  end
  Memory[("Entity memory<br/>on the gateway host")]

  SPA -- "GET /, assets" --> Static
  SPA -- "sign in" --> Proxy
  SPA -- "/api/gateway/* (cookies)" --> Proxy
  SPA --> Host
  Proxy -- "session headers" --> Entities
  Proxy --> Meets
  Proxy --> Sessions
  Proxy --> Embed
  Proxy --> Docs
  Proxy --> About
  Proxy --> Voice
  Entities --> Memory
```

The browser talks only to the `abstractentity` server; the proxy swaps the
session cookies for gateway credentials. With `@abstractframework/app-server`
0.1.10 or newer, every request the proxy sends to the gateway also carries the
browser's own address (`X-Forwarded-For`, set from the connection and never
taken from the browser) and the marker
`X-AbstractFramework-App-Proxy: abstractentity`; see
[SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md#session-model). A `?gateway=` link to a gateway on
another origin uses a direct posture instead: the app keeps the verified token
in memory for the tab and calls the gateway directly.

## Entity routes used by the app

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as You
  participant A as Entity app
  participant G as AbstractGateway
  U->>A: open the app (or the new-entity link)
  A->>G: POST /api/gateway/entities/auth/probe
  A->>G: GET /api/gateway/entities
  alt no entity yet
    A-->>U: "No entities yet" + Create your first entity
  end
  U->>A: name "Pollux", Create entity
  A->>G: POST /api/gateway/entities (name, framework)
  G-->>A: created (or already exists)
  A->>G: GET /entities/Pollux/replay (NDJSON)
  A->>G: GET /entities/Pollux/replay/stream (SSE live tail)
  U->>A: say hello in Chat
  A->>G: POST /entities/Pollux/visit/open, then visit turns
```

All entity paths above sit under `/api/gateway`. The per-entity routes the app
reads or writes are listed in [API and configuration](api.md#gateway-routes-the-app-uses).

## The replay-stream fold

The memory engine writes an append-only replay stream of envelopes (form,
recall, commit, appraise, diary, valence, maintenance, plus gateway host
markers). The app folds this stream into its picture of a life:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R["GET replay (bounded NDJSON)"] --> N[normalizeEnvelope]
  T["GET replay/stream (SSE tail)"] --> N
  C["IndexedDB life cache"] --> N
  N --> F["applyEnvelope (pure fold)"]
  F --> S["FoldState at scrub position T"]
  S --> V["Graph · Detail · Book · Lessons · World · Health · Ledger · Cognitive Monitor"]
```

The state at any position is the fold of every envelope up to it, so replay,
live tail and time scrub are one code path, and every tab agrees at any
position.

## Where a memory comes from

Every memory an entity forms is tied to the ledger that recorded the moment
(AbstractMemory ADR 0003, 2026-10-27): the run and ledger row `(run_id, seq)` of
the step that formed it, the verbatim artifact it was digested from, the
hash-chained diary entry it projects, or the memories it was derived from, whose
own sources reach the ledger. AbstractMemory keeps the references and the
revision history ("reconsidered on, superseded by"); AbstractRuntime's memory
facade rebuilds the verbatim from them, or answers `source_gone` when a run or
artifact has been deleted; the gateway serves both under `/api/gateway/memory/`.
The app only reads: see the proposed item
[Every memory names its ledger sources](backlog/proposed/2026-10-27_memory_sources_from_the_ledger.md).

## Scope of this repository

This repository ships the Entity app. The services that make entities live
(entity homes, visit workflows, lifecycle phases, sleep and dreams, skills) run
in AbstractGateway, AbstractRuntime and AbstractMemory, and the app uses them
over HTTP. This repository also holds two shared specifications those services
read: the lifecycle phase graph ([`spec/entity_phases.json`](../spec/entity_phases.json),
explained in [The entity life cycle](entity-phases.md)) and the cognition map of
how an entity's memory is built ([`spec/cognition_graph.json`](../spec/cognition_graph.json)).
AbstractGateway serves both (`GET /api/gateway/entities/spec/phases` and
`/spec/cognition-graph`). The app reads only the phase graph, to compare the
served copy with the one it was built with: the status line beside the phase bar
says "phase rules modulated" when the operator has edited its dials and "phase
rules drift" when the two copies disagree (`spec_sync.ts`).

| Panels | `inspector.tsx`, `identity_card.tsx` + `self_brief.tsx` (his self-knowledge brief on the Card tab), `timeline.tsx` (the transport, **Live** and the **Monitor** toggle), `ledger_panel.tsx`, `ledger_lines.ts`, `turn_detail_modal.tsx`, `verbatim_modal.tsx`, `phase_time.ts`, `files_view.tsx` (the **Files** button: Settings → Files in a dialog of its own) |

Shares the chat's composer and execution paths; does not read private life envelopes for public text. |

| Sign-in | `connect_gateway_modal.tsx`, `gateway_session.ts` |

## Invariants

The test suite pins these:

- **State at T is a pure fold.** Replay, live tail and scrub share one code
  path; rendering only reads the fold.
- **Two id namespaces.** Bindings use graph ids, usage events use row ids; the
  fold joins them only on `display.graph_id`.
- **Diary redaction is never reconstructed.** The engine's
  `{"redacted":"diary"}` display block is the only source; a sealed entry's
  words never enter any view or feed.
- **Tool claims come from data, never prose.** Tool use renders from
  `tools_used` attributes and host events only.
- **Spatial memory is durable.** Graph layout anchors are persisted per entity,
  never derived from the camera.
- **Kind vocabulary stays in sync.** `ENGINE_RECORD_KINDS` mirrors
  `abstractmemory.MEMORY_RECORD_KINDS`; a drift test fails when a kind would
  render as unknown.
- **A malformed stream line never breaks the app.** `normalizeEnvelope` guards
  every ingest boundary and each envelope is folded under its own guard.
- **Embedding spaces are never crossed silently.** The Cognitive Monitor scores
  only with the entity's own embedder; a mismatch is refused with a message.
- **A refusal is a sentence, never a JSON body.** Every gateway refusal shows
  its `detail` (`refusalDetail`), never the raw `{"detail": …}` text. A gateway
  with no embedding route (503 on `POST /embeddings`) gives the Cognitive
  Monitor one line — "Embeddings are not configured on this gateway, so the
  cognitive monitor cannot run." — and a **Set up embeddings** link to the
  gateway console's Multimodal page (`/console#defaults`, on the proxied
  gateway when the app runs behind its proxy).

## Serving

```text
abstractentity (bin/cli.js → bin/server.js, :3007; /apps/entity/ through the gateway)
  ├─ /                      the Entity app (SPA fallback for unknown paths)
  ├─ /entity.html           302 → ./  (older bookmarks)
  ├─ /app/host              {"lan_ip": ...} for entity handles
  ├─ /api/connection/*      sign-in (HttpOnly session cookies)
  └─ /api/*                 proxied to the gateway with session headers
```

`npm run dev` mounts the same sign-in proxy in the Vite dev server, so sign-in
behaves the same in development and production.

The server follows the `@abstractframework/app-server` mount contract, so the
same build serves at `/` on its own port and behind the gateway's
`/apps/entity/`:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    B[Browser] -- "/apps/entity/…" --> G[AbstractGateway<br/>app proxy]
    G -- "path without /apps/entity<br/>X-Forwarded-Prefix / -For / -Host / -Proto" --> S["bin/server.js<br/>(127.0.0.1)"]
    S -- "X-AbstractFramework-App: entity; mount=1<br/>&lt;base href=/apps/entity/&gt;<br/>cookies Path=/apps/entity/" --> G
    S -- "api/gateway/* (session proxy)" --> GW[(gateway API)]
```

The page gets `<base href>` and `base_path` from the server; the build uses
relative asset URLs (Vite `base: "./"`); every same-origin request is relative
(`api/gateway/…` through the ui-kit `joinBaseUrl`, `api/connection/gateway`,
`app/host`, `demo/…`); and `npm run build` fails on any root-absolute
same-origin URL in `dist/` (`scripts/check_relative_urls.mjs`).

<!-- SOURCE: docs/api.md -->

# API and configuration

AbstractEntity is an app, not a library: it has no importable JavaScript API.
Its public surface is the `abstractentity` command, its environment variables,
the app's URLs, the routes its server exposes, and the AbstractGateway routes it
calls. This page is the reference for all of them. For a guided first run, see
[Getting started](getting-started.md); for how the pieces fit, see
[Architecture](architecture.md).

## Command

```bash
npx @abstractframework/entity      # run without installing
abstractentity                     # after npm install -g @abstractframework/entity
```

The command serves the built app and the sign-in proxy, prints the local address
and the gateway it fronts (and where that address came from), and stops on
Ctrl+C. `abstractentity --help` lists the launch flags; an unknown flag stops
the start with exit code 2.

## Configuration

| Launch flag | Default | Purpose | Legacy environment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--gateway-url <url>` (aliases `--gateway`, `--url`) | the gateway installed on this computer (`~/.abstractframework/gateway.json`), else `http://127.0.0.1:8080` | The gateway this deployment fronts; the sign-in dialog defaults to it | `ABSTRACTENTITY_GATEWAY_URL`, `ABSTRACTGATEWAY_URL` |
| `--port <n>` | `3007` | Port the server listens on | `PORT` |
| `--host <addr>` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address. Loopback by default; `--host 0.0.0.0` exposes the app on your network | `HOST` |

A launch flag wins over its legacy environment variable. With neither, the app
uses the gateway installed on this computer: `abstractgateway serve` and the
AbstractFramework installer record its address in
`~/.abstractframework/gateway.json`. A running app re-reads that file when the
gateway refuses a connection, so it follows a gateway that moved to another
port; a gateway URL you chose never moves.

### Serving through the gateway (`/apps/entity/`)

A gateway that manages the Entity app serves it at `/apps/entity/` on the
gateway's own address and starts it on `127.0.0.1`. Nothing needs
configuring: the same build serves at `/` on the app's own port and at
`/apps/entity/` through the gateway. The page is served with
`<base href="/apps/entity/">`, every asset and request is relative to the page,
the session cookies carry `Path=/apps/entity/`, and every response carries
`X-AbstractFramework-App: entity; mount=1`. The app URLs below work under
either address. Serving under `/apps/entity/` needs AbstractGateway 0.7.0 or
newer.

The sign-in proxy (`@abstractframework/app-server`) reads its own
`ABSTRACTENTITY_*` / `ABSTRACTGATEWAY_*` settings, for example whether the
browser may change the gateway URL from a non-loopback host; see the
AbstractUIC `app-server` documentation.

## App URLs

| URL | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | The entities list (or **No entities yet** with **Create your first entity**) |
| `/#new` (also `/#/new`) | The entities list with the creation form open; the fragment is cleared when the form closes |
| `/?entity=NAME` | One entity's page, starting on its live present |
| `/?entity=NAME&live=0` | One entity's page, replaying its life from the start |
| `/?gateway=URL&entity=NAME` | One entity on a gateway at another origin (direct sign-in, token kept in memory for the tab) |
| `/?src=URL` | Any exported replay stream (NDJSON) loaded as a read-only life |

With no `entity` or `src` parameter and no reachable gateway, the app opens the
bundled demo life.

## Server routes

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/connection/gateway` | Sign in: exchanges a gateway token for a session held in HttpOnly cookies (`abstractentity_gateway_*`) |
| `/api/gateway/*` | Proxied to the gateway with the session's credentials; mutating calls need the CSRF header |
| `GET /app/host` | `{"lan_ip": "..."}`: the machine's first non-internal IPv4 address (or `null`), used for entity handles such as `pollux@192.168.1.20` |
| `GET /entity.html` | Redirects to the app's home (`./`, keeping the query) |
| any other path | A file from `dist/`, else the app (SPA fallback) |

## Gateway routes the app uses

All paths are under `/api/gateway`. The app works against whatever subset the
gateway serves; a surface whose route is missing shows a labelled gap instead
of invented data.

| Family | Routes |
| --- | --- |
| Entities | `GET /entities` (list; also the names offered by `@` in a conversation), `POST /entities` (create: `name`, optional `spark_text`, `framework`), `POST /entities/auth/probe` |
| Life stream | `GET /entities/{name}/replay` (NDJSON), `GET /entities/{name}/replay/stream` (SSE) |
| Records | `GET /entities/{name}/records/{id}/verbatim`, `GET /entities/{name}/diary/{id}` |
| Life cycle | `GET /entities/{name}/life_state`, `PUT /entities/{name}/life_state/toggles`, `POST /entities/{name}/lifecycle`, `POST /entities/{name}/state` (sleep now); `GET /entities/{name}/loop` and `/seat` (reads); `GET /entities/spec/phases` (the served phase graph, compared with the bundled copy for the "phase rules" notes). See [Life cycle](#life-cycle-the-phase-bar) |
| Card and metrics | `/entities/{name}/tile` (the home grid draws each entity with the ui-kit `EntityCard` from `GET /entities`, whose rows carry `state`, then reads tiles three at a time once that entity's `/loop` and `life_state` answered, kept until 5 minutes pass, the row's `state.changed_at` moves or the served phase's `rev` moves; the card's **Watch** opens the entity, **Retry** and **Resume** post `lifecycle`), `/card` (the Card tab), `/footprint`, `/cognition`, `/communities`, `/embedding` |
| Visits and chat | `/entities/{name}/visit/open`, `/visit/{run}/turn`, `/tick`, `/close`, `/transcript`, `/state`, `/guidance`, `/answer`, `/decision`, `/ledger` (the live activity panel: the visit run's records after a cursor, read once a second while a turn runs; where served it reads `topic` on each recall handle, `iteration` and `max_iterations` on the `reason` model call, and `hits` on a `search_memory` result); `/chat/open`, `/chat/{id}/turn`, `/close`, `/transcript`; `/summon`; `/queue/{id}`; `POST /sessions/{session_id}/mentions` (see [Mentions](#mentions-in-a-conversation)) |
| Settings | `/entities/{name}/substrate`, `/cognition-profile` (Settings → Mind, including the Sleep card), `/prompt`, `/tool-policy`, `/skills`, `/workspace`, `/workspace/file`, `/workspace/mounts`, `/access`; `GET /voice/voices`, `GET /voice/defaults` |
| Identity (AbstractGateway 0.20.0) | `GET /entities/{name}/identity[?rev=N]` (the record: design, colour, voice, revision; `?rev` for the history), `PUT /entities/{name}/identity` (the whole record, one Save; a refusal's `detail` is shown as it is, its `error.download` becomes the **Download** button: `POST /models/download`), `GET /entities/{name}/voice` (only its `note`, the sentence for a record without a voice) |
| Track record (AbstractGateway 0.20.0) | `GET /entities/{name}/track-record`, `/reputation`, `/acquaintances`, read when the tab opens |
| Voice in a visit | `POST /entities/{name}/voice/tts/stream` (speak a reply in the entity's own voice, sentence by sentence); `POST /attachments/upload` (the recording, into session `entity_voice_<name>`) then `POST /runs/{run}/audio/transcribe` (dictation) |
| Meets | `POST /entities/meets/open`, `/entities/meets/{id}/relay`, `/close`, `GET /entities/meets/{id}` |
| Other | `POST /embeddings` (the Cognitive Monitor; 503 = no embedding route: the monitor says so and links to the console's Multimodal page), `/docs/corpus` (top-bar assistant), `GET /about` (versions in the About dialog) |

### Life cycle (the phase bar)

The phase bar ([The entity life cycle](entity-phases.md)) uses one read, three
writes and the live stream. Every path is under `/api/gateway/entities/{name}`.

| Call | Body | What the app does with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /life_state` | none | Draws the bar: `phase` (`idle`, `personal`, `work`, `visit`, `sleep` or `stopped`), `stopped`, `toggles: {personal}`, `since`, `sentence`, `next: {phase, sentence}`, `blocked: {code, sentence, action}`, `can: {visit, sleep_now, toggle_personal}` (each `{allowed, sentence}`), `visit`, `work: {jobs_queued, current: {kind, run_id, since}}`, `sleep: {kind, reason, since, ends}`, `rev` and `generation` |
| `PUT /life_state/toggles` | `{"personal": true}` or `{"personal": false}` | Grants or takes back own time. The app never sends `work`: there is no work switch, and the gateway refuses it (422 `unknown_field`) |
| `POST /lifecycle` | `{"action": "stop"}`, `{"action": "resume"}` or `{"action": "retry"}` | Stop (it also revokes own time), Resume (back to idle), Retry (start own time again when `blocked.action` is `retry`). A stop's answer lists what it did in `items`, each with its `sentence`; `complete: false` keeps a second Stop beside Resume |
| `POST /state` | `{"state": "sleep", "dream": true}` | Sleep now: the entity sleeps for its maintenance and wakes when it is done. The app does not wait on this call; the stream shows the sleep and the wake. The chat also sends `{"state": "awake"}` once, before retrying, when an older visit door refuses a visit because the entity is asleep |

- **Live.** A host event with `payload.kind == "phase_changed"` on
  `GET /replay/stream` repaints the bar at once; the app then reads
  `life_state` again. The bar also re-reads every 15 seconds.
- **Newest wins.** The answer with the highest `rev` wins, and an answer from
  before a Stop (a lower `generation`) never repaints the bar after it.
- **Refusals.** A refusal's `detail.message` is shown as it is, and its
  `detail.life_state` (when present) repaints the bar. Coded refusals without
  a message get the app's sentence for the code: `stopped_use_resume`,
  `in_visit`, `already_asleep`, `entity_archived`, `unknown_field`,
  `invalid_body`, `invalid_toggles`, `invalid_action` and `entity_not_found`.
  `admin_required` always reads "Only an admin can grant his own time, stop or
  resume him."
- **Older gateways.** A `life_state` answer without these fields (no `rev`,
  no `can`, no `generation`, or a `work` that is not the job queue) shows "This
  gateway does not serve the phase bar yet." with every control off. The app
  never falls back to older routes.
- **Sleep thresholds.** Settings → Mind → Sleep reads `GET /cognition-profile`
  and saves one field at a time with `PUT /cognition-profile`:
  `{"sleep": {"after_hours": 48}}`, `{"sleep": {"after_events": 500}}`
  (integers of at least 1; hours at most 720) or
  `{"sleep": {"after_fragmented_share": 0.2}}` (a share above 0 and at most 1;
  the field shows and takes it as a percentage, 20). The answer is the whole
  profile. A refusal shows the gateway's sentence under the field. A profile
  without a `sleep` block shows "This gateway does not offer the sleep
  settings yet." and disables the three fields; a `sleep` block without
  `after_fragmented_share` shows "This gateway does not offer this sleep
  setting yet." under that field and disables it alone.

### His topics (the graph's layout)

The graph reads his topics with `GET /api/gateway/entities/{name}/communities`.
The app reads payload version 2 as memory serves it: `version`, `version_seq`,
`first_sleep_pending`, `algorithm`, `communities` (each with `id`, `key`,
`title`, `summary`, `pending`, `verdict`, `size`, `kinds`, `members`,
`provisional_ids`, `cohesion`, `layout: {xy, radius, seats}`,
`centroid_stale` and `facts`, whose fields may each be absent) and `links`.

- **Layout.** Each topic is a circle at `layout.xy` with `layout.radius`, and
  each member sits on its seat. A topic's `key` stays the same from one
  version to the next, so your focus, its colour and where you dragged it
  survive a new version; `id` names the current revision.
- **Titles and summaries** are memory's own: "title being written…" while
  `pending` says so, never a label the app makes up. A `verdict` of
  `no_common_subject` reads "He found no common subject in these memories."
- **Live.** A host event with `payload.kind == "communities_changed"` on
  `GET /replay/stream` makes the graph read the new version once; a `placed`
  event seats a new memory in its topic at once, with the badge "placed until
  his next sleep".
- **The chat names them too.** The live activity panel's recall row adds the
  titles of the topics most of the recalled memories are in (each recall
  handle's `topic` in the visit ledger, matched to `key` here; never the key
  itself). It reads this route once when a turn names a topic whose title it
  does not hold, at most once per turn.
- **Before his first sleep** (`first_sleep_pending`) the graph uses its plain
  layout and says "His topics form during his next sleep."
- **Older gateways.** An answer without `version` 2, or one that leaves out a
  required field, shows "This gateway does not serve topics yet." and the
  plain layout; the app never works out topics itself.

### Replies, badges and cut summaries

- **Badges.** What a turn formed is served beside the reply, never inside its
  words: `reply_notices` on a visit turn's answer, and `notices` on a
  flow-brain answer in the replay view. Each notice is one badge under the
  reply; a click opens its record.
- **Cut summaries.** When the gateway marks a record `cut: true` (the record
  read, the replay's record and recall blocks, and the statements of
  `GET /card`), the app shows the record's title and "Older record: its
  summary was cut when saved; he rewrites it in his sleep." instead of the
  cut words. Without the flag, the words show as stored.
- **A Stop during an open.** A visit open answered with 409
  `stopped_use_resume` shows the gateway's sentence and **Resume and visit**.

### Mentions in a conversation

In a visit, or a flow-brain conversation, `@` lists the entities that
`GET /entities` returns for your account, except the one you are talking to.
A pick becomes a chip; the app never reads `@` out of the typed words. On send,
your message goes out as usual, then each mention, in the order you picked it
and each only after the previous one answered:

```http
POST /api/gateway/sessions/{session_id}/mentions
{"entity": "nerin", "text": "<your message as typed>", "mention_index": 0,
 "repeat_of": "<your turn in this session, flow-brain lane only>",
 "mention_id": "<message>:<entity>:<mention_index>"}
```

- **`mention_id`** names one mention of one message. The message part is your
  own turn in the session (`repeat_of`) or, in a visit, an id the app makes
  once for the message (`msg-` and 24 hex digits) and keeps for a resend. When
  you send the same words again after a failure, the same ids go out and the
  gateway returns the answer the entity already gave instead of asking it
  twice.
- **200**: `reply` is shown as its own message, labelled from `author`
  (`{kind, name, entity_id, identity_ref, avatar}`): the entity's avatar, its
  name and an "entity" tag. `mirrors` lists the visits that were also told
  the reply (in a visit, the entity you are visiting); the app adds "Also said
  to Castor." under the answer.
- **409** (`in_another_conversation`, or another refusal from the visit
  door): "Pollux is in another conversation." (or the gateway's sentence), and
  the next mention goes on.
- **503**: the gateway's sentence; your words and the chips that were not
  answered go back to the message box. Sending the same words again asks only
  those entities.
- **404 `entity_not_found`**: "Pollux cannot be mentioned here."; the name is
  no longer offered.
- **422 `repeat_of_unknown`**: the gateway's sentence; your message goes back
  to the message box.
- **404 or 405 without a code**: the gateway has no mentions route. The app
  says "This gateway does not offer mentions yet" and from then on `@` shows
  that sentence instead of names.

In the flow-brain lane, the turn itself also names the chips:
`POST /entities/{name}/summon` carries `mentions` (the picked entities'
slugs, in pick order, each once), so the entity knows the mentioned entities
answer for themselves. A message without chips sends no `mentions`.

The app sets no time limit on a mention, as on any visit turn.

### Avatar conversation

The optional Avatar presentation needs AbstractGateway 0.19.0 or newer. It requests
`conversation: true` on a new durable visit's open body. Existing visits keep their initial mode. The app reads only
`GET /entities/{name}/visit/{run}/state` public fields: `public_updates`,
`public_messages`, `public_questions`, `pending_question` and `pending_wait`. It does not derive
public speech from the entity's private replay envelopes or technical output.

`public_questions` carries canonical question, real user answer, system expiry and
retained-reply messages with their original run/question identity and source.
An expiry fallback stays a system outcome; it is never rendered as a person answering.
Public arrays merge by the gateway's recorded `order` and `published_at`, not a
browser-time estimate. Each of the three public arrays is bounded to 64 messages,
with at most 32 runs in the visit tree inspected. Positive `public_updates_omitted`,
`public_messages_omitted`, `public_questions_omitted` or `conversation_runs_omitted`
shows the earlier-exchanges notice. These bounds limit the view, not durable storage.

During a durable visit, `POST /guidance` under that visit sends
`{text, display_text}`: `text` may quote a selected public update, while
`display_text` is the person's own words for public history. Its accepted receipt
means the guidance is available, not that the actor adopted it. A pending question
uses `POST /answer` with `{wait_key, response, target_run_id}` from that exact
question. Permission controls use `POST /decision` with `{wait_key, approved}`;
silence does not grant permission. A refusal keeps the draft for retry.

The Flow-brain lane is a separate summoned workflow in the authenticated
principal's runtime. Avatar turns request
`input_data._runtime.conversation.enabled: true`. Its existing served run view
provides explicit public messages and interactions; supported workflow commands
carry live guidance or an exact wait response. Durable visit runs use their owned
visit routes and never fall through to those generic commands.

Essential questions wait for an answer. Clarifications show the server's deadline
and declared fallback. Visual and audio cues are both on; the view has no cue
settings. Public-update narration uses the
listener's read-aloud preference and the entity voice described below. Opening,
history restoration, reconnects and hidden conversation panels establish silent
baselines.

### Identity and track record

Settings → identity is the ui-kit's `IdentityPanel` (look, voice, history, one Save at the bottom),
wired to this gateway in `identity_settings.tsx`. It reads `GET /entities/{name}/identity` and
saves the whole record with one `PUT` (`{avatar: {style, color}, voice: {provider, model, voice}}`;
the record's speed and quality ride along while the voice is unchanged; a voice chosen without its
speech model takes the model a cloned voice is bound to, else the engine's first listed model). The
voices come from `GET voice/voices`; choosing one plays a short sample on the entity's own lane
(`POST /entities/{name}/voice/tts/stream` with the chosen voice fields: nothing is saved); **Create a
new voice** uses `POST voice/design` or `POST voice/clones`. The design list is the AbstractAvatar catalog bundled in
the ui-kit, limited to designs with a Watch code (the gateway refuses the others). The avatar draws
the design in the entity's colour: the colour replaces the theme's `--warning` token around the
canvas, the body colour of the kit's palette. A refusal is shown word for word and nothing is
retried. History reads `?rev=N` for every revision, newest first. A record without a voice shows
the `note` of `GET /entities/{name}/voice`, the gateway's sentence.

The Avatar view resolves the visit's `identity_ref` (from `POST /visit/open`, or the newest public
update that carries one) with `GET /entities/{name}/identity?rev=N`. A visit that names no identity
(a visit rejoined after a reload before any update arrives, a Flow conversation) draws the kit's
avatar.

Settings → track record shows the gateway's numbers as they are; the words are the app's: a trust
cell with no outcome reads "No experience yet", and the `completion-rate only` basis reads "A
success here only means the task finished: nobody has judged the quality of the work yet."

### Voice uses the same gateway routes

Voice uses the same gateway routes and ui-kit components as AbstractCode. It
needs AbstractGateway 0.13.0 or later (`GET /voice/defaults`):

- **Speak.** A reply's speaker button, or **Read aloud**, posts the reply to the
  entity-owned streaming lane. The request carries the text and, when set, the
  listener's latency choice — never a provider, model or voice: the gateway
  speaks with the entity's own voice (Settings → identity), else its `output.voice`
  default, and sends the audio one sentence at a time, so the first words play
  while the rest is synthesised. **Stop** aborts the request.
- **Dictate.** The composer microphone records in the browser (hold to dictate,
  or tap to start and tap again to stop), uploads the recording into the
  session `entity_voice_<name>` and transcribes it on the run the upload names,
  with the gateway's `input.voice` route unless you chose another. While it
  works the composer shows `Transcribing… 4 s · faster-whisper / large-v3`; a
  failure, or no answer within 180 s, shows a sentence.
- **Defaults.** "Gateway default · supertonic / supertonic-3" and the
  transcription route come from `GET /voice/defaults`, never from the voice
  catalog's engine fields.

The replay stream format and the gateway routes are owned by AbstractMemory and
AbstractGateway; see their documentation for request and response shapes.

## Specifications in this repository

- [`spec/entity_phases.json`](../spec/entity_phases.json): the entity life
  cycle's phase graph (version 25), served by the gateway at
  `GET /api/gateway/entities/spec/phases`. Human-readable companion:
  [The entity life cycle](entity-phases.md).
- [`spec/cognition_graph.json`](../spec/cognition_graph.json): the cognition map
  of how an entity's memory is built, served by the gateway at
  `GET /api/gateway/entities/spec/cognition-graph`. The app does not draw it.

## Related

- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) for sign-in, gateway and port problems.
- [Data flow](DataFlow.md) for which route feeds which surface.
