# FAQ

## What is an entity?

An AI companion with a lasting memory of its own that lives on your
AbstractGateway. See [What is an entity?](../README.md#what-is-an-entity).

## Where is an entity's memory stored?

On the gateway host, in the entity's own folder. AbstractEntity stores no
entity data on its server. The browser keeps a local cache of replay streams
(IndexedDB) so large lives reopen quickly; it is only a cache of what the
gateway serves.

## Can I rename an entity or reuse a name?

A name belongs to one entity for its whole life. Creating an entity with an
existing name opens the existing entity; it does not create a new one from a
different starting document.

## What is the starting document?

The document an entity is created from: its name and initial identity. With just
a name, the gateway uses the standard starting document with the name filled
in. **Advanced: starting document** on the creation form accepts your own YAML;
it is stored exactly as written.

## Does watching an entity change it?

No. The entities list, states, cards and memory views are read-only. Actions
such as granting its own time, putting it to sleep or stopping it go through
the gateway and appear as visible events in the entity's life.

## What does an entity do when nobody talks to it?

It stays **idle**, awake and visitable, unless you grant it its own time with
the **personal** toggle; jobs queued for it are worked on either way. While it
is idle, once 24 hours have passed since its last sleep, or it has formed 500
new memories since then, it sleeps for maintenance and comes back idle. See
[The entity life cycle](entity-phases.md).

## What does the Cognitive Monitor measure?

The expressive character of the entity's own words (visit replies, diary,
summaries), scored against a fixed basis with the entity's own embedding model.
It does not measure inner state, and sealed diary entries are never read. Open
it with **Monitor**, after **Live** in the timeline's controls: it docks under
the graph and reads his words at the timeline's position (**read his words**
scores them) or, live with the chat open, the reply in view.

## How do I read the graph's colours?

Grey to green is how often he used a memory or a pair of memories; amber is a
pair he used together a moment ago; after a reply, gold, pink and blue rings
say why each recalled memory came (present by right, continuity, matched). See
[Reading the memory graph](../README.md#reading-the-memory-graph).

## Why is some diary text hidden?

Sealed diary entries stay sealed in every view. The app shows that an entry
exists but never reconstructs its words.

## Do I need AbstractObserver?

No. AbstractEntity runs on its own against AbstractGateway. AbstractObserver is
a separate app for runs and gateway activity.

## Which gateway version do I need?

The app works with any AbstractGateway; surfaces whose route the gateway does
not serve show a labelled gap. The gateway console's **Create your first
entity** shortcut needs AbstractGateway 0.4.1 or newer. The optional Avatar
conversation (public updates, corrections and question answers during a visit)
needs AbstractGateway 0.19.0 or newer. The five-state phase bar, Settings →
Mind (with its Sleep card), `@` mentions, reply badges and his topics need
AbstractGateway 0.21.0 or newer; with an older one the app says "This gateway
does not serve the phase bar yet.", "This gateway does not offer mentions
yet" or "This gateway does not serve topics yet." instead, and replies show
no badges.

## How do I see which versions I am running?

Open **About** (the info button at the top right). It is one short card: the
app's name and version, the **AbstractFramework** and **AbstractGateway**
versions, links to the website, source, documentation, issue tracker, feedback
and contact, and the author and licence line. It does not list packages. Each
time the card opens, the app asks the connected gateway for its versions
(`GET /api/gateway/about`); the AbstractGateway line reads:

- **checking…** while the answer is on its way;
- the version, for example **0.12.0**, once the gateway answers (the
  AbstractFramework line then shows the framework installed on the gateway
  host, or says it is not installed there);
- **unavailable (reason)** when the gateway cannot answer, for example
  `unavailable (HTTP 404)`;
- **not connected** when the app shows the demo life or a `?src=` stream.

The app's version is the `@abstractframework/entity` package version, fixed at
build time.

## Can I use the app without a gateway?

Yes, to explore: without a reachable gateway the app opens a bundled demo life,
and `/?src=URL` loads any exported replay stream. Creating and talking with
entities needs a gateway.

## Can I use the app on a phone or a tablet?

Yes. Below 1024 px the side panel opens as a drawer over the memory graph, and
on a phone the tabs sit in a strip along the bottom of the screen, dialogs open
from the bottom, and controls are sized for touch. See
[Responsive layout](../README.md#responsive-layout) for the details and the
limits on small screens.

For fixes to specific problems, see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).


<!-- ============================================================ -->
<!-- SOURCE: docs/troubleshooting.md -->
<!-- ============================================================ -->

# Troubleshooting

Each entry lists the symptom, how to confirm the cause, and the fix. Setup
steps are in [Getting started](getting-started.md); settings are in
[API and configuration](api.md#configuration).

## The app shows a demo life instead of my entities

**Cause:** the app could not reach a gateway, so it opened the bundled demo.

**Check:** the command prints `Gateway: <url>` on start. Confirm that gateway is
running and reachable from the machine that runs `abstractentity`.

**Fix:** start the gateway, or point the app at it with
`abstractentity --gateway-url http://HOST:PORT`, then reload the page.

## The sign-in dialog rejects my token or keeps coming back

**Check:** the gateway URL in the dialog is the gateway you expect, and the
token is a valid user token for that gateway.

**Fix:** sign in again with a valid token. If you opened a `?gateway=` link to
a gateway on another origin, the token is kept only for that tab; open the app
from its own address (`http://127.0.0.1:3007`) to use the persistent cookie
session. See [Sign-in in Architecture](architecture.md#components-and-connections).

## The gateway console has no "Create your first entity" button

**Cause:** the button comes with AbstractGateway 0.4.1 or newer.

**Fix:** upgrade the gateway, or open the app yourself at
`http://127.0.0.1:3007/#new`, which opens the same creation form.

## Creating an entity opens an existing one

**Cause:** the name is already taken. A name belongs to one entity for life
(see the [FAQ](faq.md#can-i-rename-an-entity-or-reuse-a-name)).

**Fix:** choose a different name.

## Creating an entity with my own starting document is refused

**Cause:** with the **Framework check** switch on (the default), the gateway requires the `shared_vulnerability` core value in the
starting document.

**Fix:** add that value to your document, or switch **Framework check** off in
**Advanced: starting document** if you deliberately want to skip it.

## A panel shows a gap instead of data

**Cause:** the gateway does not serve that route (for example the on-disk
footprint in **Health**). The app labels the gap rather than estimating.

**Fix:** upgrade the gateway to a version that serves the route; see
[Gateway routes the app uses](api.md#gateway-routes-the-app-uses).

## The phase bar says "This gateway does not serve the phase bar yet."

**Cause:** the gateway does not serve the five-state life cycle (idle, own
time, work, visit, sleep, with the job queue). The bar's controls stay off
rather than guessing.

**Fix:** upgrade the gateway to AbstractGateway 0.21.0 or newer. See
[Life cycle (the phase bar)](api.md#life-cycle-the-phase-bar).

## The phase bar shows "His own time stopped unexpectedly"

**Cause:** its own time is granted, but nothing is running.

**Fix:** press **Retry** beside the sentence. To stop granting it instead,
turn **personal** off; the entity stays awake.

## Typing `@` says "This gateway does not offer mentions yet"

**Cause:** the gateway has no mentions route.

**Fix:** upgrade the gateway to AbstractGateway 0.21.0 or newer. Until then,
talk with each entity in its own visit, or convene a meet from the entities
list.

## The graph shows no topics

**Cause:** before his first sleep, his memory has not formed topics yet: the
graph uses its plain layout and says "His topics form during his next sleep."
With a gateway that does not serve topics, it says "This gateway does not
serve topics yet."

**Fix:** wait for his next sleep (or put him to sleep with **sleep now**), or
upgrade the gateway to AbstractGateway 0.21.0 or newer. See
[His topics](api.md#his-topics-the-graphs-layout).

## The Cognitive Monitor refuses to score

**Cause:** the Cognitive Monitor scores only with the entity's own embedding
model; if the gateway's embeddings do not match the scorer's basis, or the
gateway has no embedding endpoint, the monitor stops with an explanation rather
than showing invented scores.

**Fix:** make sure the gateway serves `/api/gateway/embeddings` with the model
the entity was created with. The rest of the app is unaffected.

## The Cognitive Monitor says "Embeddings are not configured on this gateway"

**Cause:** the gateway has no embedding route, so `POST /api/gateway/embeddings`
answers 503 and the monitor cannot score. The monitor shows "Embeddings are not
configured on this gateway, so the cognitive monitor cannot run." and a
**Set up embeddings** link.

**Fix:** follow **Set up embeddings**; it opens the gateway console's
Multimodal page (`/console#defaults`), where an administrator sets the
embedding route. Reopen the entity page afterwards; the monitor scores again.
The rest of the app works without embeddings.

## About shows "AbstractGateway: unavailable (…)"

**Cause:** the app could not read `GET /api/gateway/about`. The reason in
brackets tells you why: `HTTP 404` means the gateway does not serve the About
route, and `not a gateway response` means no gateway answered behind the app's
address.

**Fix:** check that the gateway is running (see the first entry above), or
upgrade it to a version that serves `GET /about`. The rest of the app is unaffected; see
[the FAQ](faq.md#how-do-i-see-which-versions-i-am-running).

## The port is already in use

**Fix:** start on another port with `abstractentity --port 3017`.

## Other devices on my network cannot open the app

**Cause:** the server binds to `127.0.0.1` by default.

**Fix:** open it through your gateway (`/apps/entity/`, one port for the
console and every app), or start it with `--host 0.0.0.0` and only on a network
you trust; see [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).

## Copy says "Copy failed — select and copy"

**Cause:** the app is open over plain `http://` from another machine (a LAN or
Tailscale address such as `http://100.x.y.z:8080/apps/entity/`). Browsers
offer the clipboard, the microphone and the camera only on https pages or on
`localhost`, so **Copy** falls back to a text-selection copy that the browser
may refuse. Everything else in the app works over plain http.

**Fix:** open the app over https or on the gateway's own computer. With
Tailscale, run `tailscale serve --bg http://127.0.0.1:<port>` on the gateway
machine and open `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net/apps/entity/`; the gateway
console's Network page explains the steps.

## `npm run build` fails in a checkout with unresolved `@abstractframework/ui-kit`

**Cause:** the dependencies are not installed yet.

**Fix:** run `npm install`, then `npm run build` again. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).


<!-- ============================================================ -->
<!-- SOURCE: docs/Overview.md -->
<!-- ============================================================ -->

# Overview

This page explains the app's goals and main parts in prose. For diagrams and
the module map, see [Architecture](architecture.md); for setup, see
[Getting started](getting-started.md).

AbstractEntity is the **summoned-entity app** for AbstractFramework: where
you create entities, watch a mind's memory live, read what it has kept, and
talk with it. It is a thin client — a static React SPA with no server state
of its own; everything renders from the gateway's HTTP endpoints and the
memory engine's frozen replay-stream format.

## Goals

- **Observe a mind honestly.** Show the memory graph, the diary, the mood,
  and the on-disk shape of a life — each from its real source, none faked.
  When something cannot be known (a redacted diary word, a byte count the
  stream doesn't carry), the app says so rather than inventing it.
- **Talk with an entity.** Visits (chat) with per-cycle visibility,
  steering, and per-phase workspace/tool grants; two entities can be
  convened into one conversation (the Meet console).
- **One code path for time.** Replay, live tail, and time-scrub are the
  same pure fold over the replay stream — the state at any position is the
  fold of every envelope up to it.

## The challenge

The memory engine emits an append-only **replay stream** (form / recall /
commit / appraise / diary / valence / maintenance envelopes, plus gateway
host markers). The app's job is to fold that stream into a faithful,
scrubbable picture of a mind — at operator scale (a handful of homes, tens
of thousands of envelopes per busy life) and without ever misrepresenting
what the engine actually recorded. The hard parts are all honesty and
resilience: two id namespaces that must join correctly, diary redaction that
must survive every render path, embedding spaces that must never be crossed
silently, and a single malformed line that must never brick the view.

## Core components

- **Stream + fold** (`stream_source.ts`, `stream_fold.ts`) — NDJSON/SSE
  ingest with `normalizeEnvelope` at every boundary; a pure incremental fold
  that yields `FoldState` (nodes, edges, standings, beats, sessions,
  attention windows) at any scrub position.
- **Memory graph** (`graph_canvas.tsx`, `graph_canvas_legend.tsx`,
  `force_layout.ts`, `graph_usage.ts`, `topic_layout.ts`, `topics_panel.tsx`)
  — the mind as a live graph laid out by the topics his memory forms in his
  sleep (force-directed until they are served), with a Topics panel you can
  move and resize (one card per topic, its memory types and paths most
  travelled), a two-line legend you click to see where a kind of memory or
  link sits, a grey-to-green usage scale ranked within each life, the Context
  view (the memories of a recall and the paths travelled to reach them), and
  durable spatial memory.
- **Reading surfaces** — **Book** (`book_reader.tsx`): the diary as a
  chronological journal; **Health** (`health_panel.tsx` + `health_metrics.ts`):
  memory-shape metrics + on-disk footprint; **Cognitive Monitor**
  (`cognition_wave_panel.tsx`, opened with **Monitor** in the timeline):
  uic's text-mood instrument, docked under the graph.
- **Visits** (`chat_drawer.tsx`, `workspace_panel.tsx`) — turns with cycle
  visibility, steering, per-phase grants; the fabricated-liveness guard.
- **Meets** (`meet_reader.tsx`, `meet_console.tsx`) — read a past shared
  moment; convene/relay/close a live two-entity conversation.
- **Entities list + auth** (`entities_index.tsx`, `create_entity_form.tsx`,
  `fleet_view.tsx`, `connect_gateway_modal.tsx`) — the list with its
  first-run empty state and creation form, the watch-all wall, and the shared
  app-origin session sign-in.

## What lives elsewhere

The services that make entities *live* (entity homes, visit workflows,
lifecycle phases, sleep and dreams, skills) run in AbstractGateway,
AbstractRuntime and AbstractMemory; this app uses them over HTTP. See
[Architecture](architecture.md#scope-of-this-repository).

## Honesty invariants

These are load-bearing and test-pinned:

- Diary redaction is honored in the pixel path and never reconstructed; a
  sealed entry's words never enter any feed (Book, Cognitive Monitor).
- The Cognitive Monitor always carries "reads the expressive character of
  text, not inner state," and never crosses embedding spaces (the home's
  embedder pin drives scoring; a mismatch refuses loudly).
- Tool claims render from `tools_used` attributes and host events only,
  never from reply prose.
- A single malformed journal line skips with a warning; it never throws to
  the render root.
- On-disk footprint comes from the gateway's endpoint; when that route is
  absent the panel shows a labeled gap, never estimated bytes.


<!-- ============================================================ -->
<!-- SOURCE: docs/DataFlow.md -->
<!-- ============================================================ -->

# Data flow

This page is a companion to [Architecture](architecture.md). How data moves from the gateway/engine into each surface. The app holds no
server state; every view is a function of gateway responses.

## Transport + auth

```
browser ── same-origin ──▶ bin/cli.js (app-origin session proxy)
                              │  POST /api/connection/gateway  → HttpOnly cookies (url/session/csrf)
                              └─ /api/gateway/*                → proxied with session headers
          ── or direct ────▶ gateway  (cross-origin ?gateway= deep link; bearer in memory for the tab)
```

`stream_source.ts` owns the wire: `readHeaders` (bearer when present),
`proxyCsrfHeader` (mutating calls), `credentials: "include"` (cookie
posture). Local-vs-remote gateway config is gated on the socket peer in the
shared proxy, never on the client `Host` header.

## The replay-stream fold (the spine)

```
GET /entities/{name}/replay        (NDJSON, bounded)      ┐
GET /entities/{name}/replay/stream (SSE, live tail)       � ─▶ normalizeEnvelope ─▶ applyEnvelope ─▶ FoldState
scrub position T (re-fold 0..T, cached incrementally)     ┘
```

- **`normalizeEnvelope`** rejects a non-finite `seq`, coerces `payload` to
  an object, requires a string `family` — a bad line is dropped counted,
  never handed downstream.
- **`applyEnvelope`** dispatches by family (event/binding/closure/trace/
  snapshot/valence + gateway `host` markers) into `FoldState`, wrapped in a
  per-envelope guard (defense-in-depth above the panel error boundaries).
- **State-at-T** is the fold of every envelope with `seq <= T`; forward is
  incremental, backward re-folds from 0 (cheap at entity scale). Replay,
  live tail, and scrub are one path.
- **Life cache** (`replay_cache.ts`): the bounded replay is cached in
  IndexedDB per (gateway origin, entity); reopening a life paints from the
  cached prefix and fetches only `seq > cached max` (cursored delta —
  sound because the journal is append-only and marker seqs mint at journal
  high-water). A journal-head probe (`until_seq=1`) validates lineage
  first; a reborn name drops the cache. On a long life (tens of thousands
  of envelopes) this takes reopening from about 22 s cold to under 1 s warm.

Every surface below reads `FoldState` (or the same doors), so they are all
consistent at any scrub position.

## Per-surface flow

| Surface | Reads | Produces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Memory graph | `FoldState.nodes/edges` + `temporal_activation` → `graph_usage`; his topics (`GET /communities`) | canvas laid out by his topics (force-laid until they are served), legend picks, usage scale, Context paths, the Topics panel |
| Detail | selected node + `fetchRecordVerbatim` / `fetchDiaryEntry` | verbatim, feelings, associations |
| Book | `FoldState` diary nodes (`selectDiaryEntries`) | day-grouped journal → diary door on click |
| Health | `computeHealthMetrics(FoldState)` + `fetchEntityFootprint` | re-use / concentration / forgetting / kind mix + on-disk bytes |
| Cognitive Monitor | `harvestUtterances` → `embedTexts` → vendored scorer, at the timeline's position; live with the chat open, the reply in view | scored samples → the bloom |
| Ledger | `FoldState` beats/host markers (`ledgerLine`) | the continuous life ledger |
| Meet console | `openMeet` / `relayMeet` / `closeMeet` / `fetchMeetStatus` | live two-leg transcript |

## The Cognitive Monitor pipeline (the one multi-step seam)

The Cognitive Monitor, opened with **Monitor** in the timeline and docked under
the graph, is the only surface whose data is not a direct fold read — it is a
feed the app owns feeding a scorer uic owns. It reads only while it is open,
and his words at the timeline's position only when you press **read his
words**:

```
FoldState + chat transcript
   │  utterance_harvest.ts   (entity's OWN words only: visit replies, diary, episode/summary;
   │                           sealed diary NEVER read; reply-only, chronological)
   ▼
Utterance[] { id, label, text, at, source }
   │  cognition_adapter.ts
   │    ├─ fetchEntityEmbedding  → the home's M1 embedder id (never assumed)
   │    ├─ embedTexts (gateway /embeddings, pinned to that id)  → vectors
   │    └─ scorer.score(vector)  (vendored createScorer + frozen basis_v0)
   ▼
ScoredSample[] { scores, emotions, novelty, ... }
   │  cognition_wave_panel.tsx  (the ui-kit's AfCognitionBloom)
   ▼
the bloom — framing label always on; wandering labeled session-relative
```

Guarantees end to end: a pin↔basis embedder mismatch refuses loudly
(`CognitionSpaceError`), a vectorless/failed utterance drops with a warning
(never fabricated scores), and the whole thing degrades to an explicit
message with no gateway, no utterances, or an embed failure. The vendored
`src/vendor/cognition/` is a temporary copy pending uic's
`@abstractframework/monitor-cognition` kit package; the swap is one import.

## Truth sources at a glance

- **Behavior over time** → the replay stream (graph, book, ledger, health
  metrics).
- **Disk at rest** → the gateway footprint endpoint (health "on disk").
- **Words behind a memory** → the verbatim/diary operator doors.
- **Expressive character of words** → the Cognitive Monitor's scorer (never
  presented as inner state).
- **Live conversation** → the gateway chat/meets APIs.


<!-- ============================================================ -->
<!-- SOURCE: docs/entity-phases.md -->
<!-- ============================================================ -->

# The entity life cycle

An entity is always in one of five states: **idle**, **personal** (its own
time), **work**, **visit** or **sleep**. You can also **stop** it, which halts
everything until you resume it. The bar at the top of an entity's page, the
phase bar, shows where it is now, what comes next and what you may do.

This page explains the states, what moves an entity from one to another, and
how to read the bar. In it, *you* are the entity's guardian: the person who
looks after it. Granting own time, Stop, Resume and Retry need an admin
account; with another account the bar answers "Only an admin can grant his own
time, stop or resume him." The app speaks of an entity as "he" in its
sentences; this page quotes them as they appear.

## The five states

| State | What the entity does | How it gets there | When it ends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **idle** | Awake and reachable, with nothing to do. A new entity starts here. | It is born; you resume it; a visit, its jobs or a sleep end with nothing to return to; you take its own time back. | You grant own time, a job is queued, someone visits, or it goes to sleep. |
| **personal** (own time) | Explores its own ideas, questions and interests. It may decide to sleep for maintenance and wakes by itself when the maintenance is done. | Only you grant it, with the **personal** toggle. | You take it back, or something interrupts it (a job, a visit, a sleep). |
| **work** | Works on the jobs queued for it, one after another. | A job is queued: a request from an agent, a task left with it, or its standing work order. | All its jobs are done: back to its own time if you still grant it, else idle. |
| **visit** | Talks with the person who opened the visit, and waits between turns. | Someone opens a visit, in any state except stopped. | The visit ends: back to where it was. |
| **sleep** | Maintenance: it consolidates and enriches its memory. | It decides to during its own time, it is idle and a sleep threshold is reached (see [Sleep is maintenance](#sleep-is-maintenance)), or you put it to sleep. | Its maintenance is done: back to where it was. |

When you talk with an entity yourself, that is a visit, not work.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> idle : born
    idle --> personal : you grant own time
    personal --> idle : you take it back
    idle --> work : a job is queued
    personal --> work : a job is queued
    work --> personal : jobs done, own time still granted
    work --> idle : jobs done
    idle --> sleep : 24 h or 500 memories since its last sleep, or you ask
    personal --> sleep : it decides, or you ask
    sleep --> idle : maintenance done
    sleep --> personal : maintenance done, own time still granted
    sleep --> work : maintenance done, a job waiting
```

A visit and a stop sit across every state:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    state "the state it was in" as before
    before --> visit : someone opens a visit
    visit --> before : the visit ends
    state "any state" as any
    any --> stopped : Stop
    stopped --> idle : Resume
```

## Own time is yours to give

- Only you grant or take back an entity's own time, with the **personal**
  toggle (pressed means granted). The entity never gives itself own time, and
  it never starts its own time on its own from idle.
- While you grant it, the entity explores freely, sleeps when it needs
  maintenance and wakes by itself.
- A job, a visit or a sleep interrupts its own time. When the interruption
  ends, it goes back to its own time as long as you still grant it. If you
  turned own time off in the meantime, it stays awake and idle; the bar says
  "Own time is off; he stays awake."
- Turning **personal** off never puts the entity to sleep: it finishes the
  step it is on and stays awake and visitable.
- Stop cancels its own time. After Resume it is idle until you grant own time
  again.

## Work comes from its job queue

There is no work switch. Work starts when a job is queued for the entity, from
idle or from its own time (its own time is paused while it works, then
resumes). When all its jobs are done, it goes back to its own time if you
still grant it, else it stays idle.

The **work** pill lights while the entity works and has nothing to click. Its
tooltip names the current job and since when ("Current job: summon, since
18:20.") and how many are waiting ("2 jobs queued."). The line beside the
pills shows the same count ("2 jobs queued"). When nothing runs, the tooltip
reads "Not working now. Work starts when a job is queued for him".

## Visits come back to where it was

- A visit opens in every state except stopped. Click **visit** to open the
  conversation.
- When the entity is in the middle of a step of its own or of its maintenance,
  the visit waits for it to finish that step: "waiting" shows beside
  **visit**, and the sentence reads "In a visit with Laurent; he is finishing
  what he was doing." There is no time limit, and a visit never fails because
  the entity is busy.
- A visit interrupts a sleep; it does not end it. When the visit ends, the
  same sleep continues.
- When the visit ends, the entity goes back to where it was: its own time
  (while you still grant it), its work (while jobs remain), the same sleep, or
  idle.
- While the entity is stopped, the **visit** pill offers **Resume and visit**
  after a question: "Castor is stopped. Resume him and visit? He comes back
  idle, then the conversation opens."

## Sleep is maintenance

Sleep is never "nothing": while it sleeps, the entity consolidates and
enriches its memory, and it wakes when that maintenance is done. It goes to
sleep in three ways:

- **Its own decision** during its own time, when it needs maintenance.
- **On its own while idle**, once any threshold in **Settings → Mind →
  Sleep** is reached:
  - **Sleep after (hours without sleep)**: 24 by default, from 1 to 720;
  - **Sleep after (new memories)**: 500 by default, at least 1;
  - **Sleep after (share of memories not yet settled)**: 15 % by default,
    above 0 and at most 100 %. A memory is not yet settled while it is
    placed only provisionally, has no embedding, or still waits for its
    title or summary. This one fires only once something new formed since
    the last sleep.

  The thresholds count from its last completed sleep, apply only while it is
  idle, and are checked every few minutes. The line beside the pills then
  says why it sleeps: "asleep: 24 h since the last sleep", "asleep: 500 new
  memories since the last sleep" or "asleep: 18 % of his memories are not yet
  in a topic", as the gateway words it. After such a sleep it is idle again; it
  never goes to own time that the sleep did not interrupt. Each field saves
  when you press Enter or leave it, and shows "Saved" or the reason it was
  refused. A gateway that does not offer these settings yet says "This
  gateway does not offer the sleep settings yet." and the fields stay
  disabled; one that offers the first two but not the share says "This
  gateway does not offer this sleep setting yet." under the share's field,
  which stays disabled.
- **When you ask**: click **sleep**, then answer "Put Castor to sleep now?
  He wakes by himself when his maintenance is done." with **Sleep now**. The
  bar refuses it during a visit ("He is in a visit; end it to let him
  sleep."), while the entity is already asleep ("He is already resting; a
  sleep cannot follow a sleep.") and while it is stopped.

A sleep never follows a sleep directly.

## Stop and Resume

The red **Stop** button beside the pills is the kill switch. It asks first:
"Stop Castor? Stop halts everything now and cancels his own time; after Resume
he is idle until you grant own time again." **Stop now** confirms; **Cancel**
keeps everything as it is.

- Stop halts everything at once: its own time, any work and any conversation
  in progress. Nothing new starts, and requests sent to it are turned away
  until you resume it.
- Stop is always available, even while another change you made is still on
  its way.
- After a stop the bar shows what it did, for example "Own time was
  revoked.", and the line beside the pills says it in red, for example
  "Stopped. Nothing runs until you resume him."; nothing else on the page
  moves.
  When part of the stop could not finish, the bar names it and keeps a second
  **Stop** beside **Resume** so you can try again; the entity stays stopped
  either way.
- While stopped, the **personal** toggle and **sleep** are greyed ("Stopped.
  Resume him first, then choose what he may do."), and a visit is offered
  only through **Resume and visit**.
- **Resume** brings the entity back idle, awake and visitable. Its own time
  starts again only when you grant it. A job waiting for it then moves it to
  work.

A stopped entity is not asleep: it does no maintenance and forms no memories
until you resume it.

## Every interaction forms a memory

Each turn of a visit, and each exchange during its own time or its work, forms
at least one memory, even a very short one. A visit opened and closed without a
message forms none. Sleep is when the entity consolidates what it has formed.

## Reading the phase bar

- **Five pills**: `idle`, `visit`, `work`, `personal`, `sleep`, one per state.
  The current state is lit in gold. Stopped lights no pill.
- **personal** is the one toggle. Pressed (a filled ring) means own time is
  granted. It can be pressed while another pill is lit: with **work** lit and
  **personal** pressed, its own time resumes after the jobs.
- **idle** and **work** are indicators, with nothing to click; hover idle for
  the gateway's sentence. **visit** opens the conversation; **sleep** offers
  "sleep now" and lights while the entity sleeps.
- **Stop** or **Resume**, apart from the pills.
- **Retry** appears when its own time is granted but not running, with the
  reason: "His own time stopped unexpectedly. Retry to start it again." or
  "His own time is not running. Retry to start it."
- **The line beside the pills** reads, in order: one sentence for now, since
  when in your local time (with the date when it is not today), why it sleeps,
  how many jobs are queued, and where it goes next. For example: "Working on a
  request from an agent. · since 17:09 · 2 jobs queued · then: own time". The
  last part reads "then: own time", "then: work" or "then: idle". Hover the
  line for the exact time and what happens next in words ("When his jobs are
  done, his own time resumes.").
- **Tooltips** say what each pill does, or why it cannot act now.
- **Refusals** appear in the bar as sentences.
- **The status line** between the bar and the **Files** and **Settings**
  buttons holds the page's other sentences (for example "his own time stopped
  after repeated tick failures — restart when ready", a phase-rule note or a
  sign-in note): one line, ended with "…" when it is too long, the whole
  sentence on hover. A sentence appearing or going never moves the buttons or
  the graph.

The bar follows changes as they happen and reads the entity again every 15
seconds. The tiles on the entities list show the same pills and sentence;
Stop and Resume are on the entity's own page only. A gateway that does not
serve the five-state life cycle gets one sentence, "This gateway does not
serve the phase bar yet.", and the controls stay off.

### On a phone

Below 480 px (checked at 400 px), the phase bar takes the full width of the
screen: the five state words without their icons, then **Stop**, then the
sentence and any question on lines of their own. Nothing is cut off and the
page never scrolls sideways; swipe the controls row to reach **Settings**.

## Known limits

- **Stop and work already under way.** A Stop that lands while the entity is
  in the middle of a model call can let that one call finish before
  everything halts; a maintenance step already running may finish, and a
  mention's answer already being written is not cancelled. Nothing new starts
  after the Stop. Closing this gap is planned.
- **A mention's visit.** Mentioning an entity with `@` in a conversation
  opens a visit with it for that conversation. That visit closes after 5
  minutes without a new mention; the next mention opens a new one.
- **One conversation at a time.** A visit waits, without failing, for as long
  as another person's visit with the same entity lasts.

## For contributors: the phase graph file

The machine-readable rules live in
[`spec/entity_phases.json`](../spec/entity_phases.json) (version 25), which
AbstractGateway and AbstractRuntime check themselves against and the gateway
serves; the app compares the served copy with its own and says "phase rules
drift" beside the phase bar when they differ. In that file, visit, work, personal
and sleep are the four phases of the graph, and idle and stopped are states
outside it, so no edge lands on them. When this page and the file differ,
follow the file. The routes behind the phase bar are listed in
[API and configuration](api.md#life-cycle-the-phase-bar).


<!-- ============================================================ -->
<!-- SOURCE: SECURITY.md -->
<!-- ============================================================ -->

# Security

## What the app can do

A signed-in user of AbstractEntity can create entities, talk with them, change
their model, system prompt, tool grants and workspace mounts, and start or stop
their personal time and sleep, all through the gateway. Give gateway tokens only
to people who should hold those rights.

## Session model

The `abstractentity` server uses the shared app-origin sign-in proxy
(`@abstractframework/app-server`):

- Signing in exchanges a gateway user token for a gateway session held in
  first-party HttpOnly cookies (`abstractentity_gateway_*`). The browser never
  stores the token.
- Mutating requests through the proxy require the CSRF header matching the CSRF
  cookie.
- With `@abstractframework/app-server` 0.1.10 or newer, every request the proxy
  sends to the gateway carries `X-Forwarded-For` set to the address of the
  browser's connection (a browser-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`, `Forwarded` or
  `X-Real-IP` header is dropped, never passed on) and the marker
  `X-AbstractFramework-App-Proxy: abstractentity`. The gateway uses them to tell
  whether the browser runs on the gateway's own machine. A connection whose
  address cannot be determined is refused with HTTP 400.
- A `?gateway=` link to a gateway on another origin uses a direct posture: the
  verified token is kept in memory for that tab only and is never written to
  browser storage or put in URLs.
- Tokens in URLs (`?token=`) are ignored and removed from URLs the app writes.

## Deployment defaults

- The server binds to loopback (`127.0.0.1`). To reach it from another
  machine, open it through your gateway (`/apps/entity/`, behind the gateway's
  sign-in). Binding wider with `--host` is an explicit choice; do it only on a
  network you trust, or behind your own authenticating reverse proxy.
- Behind the gateway, forwarded headers (`X-Forwarded-*`) are believed only
  from a loopback peer; a malformed one is refused with `400`.
- `GET /app/host` reports the machine's LAN IPv4 address (for entity handles)
  and nothing else.
- The Vite dev server (`npm run dev`) listens on all interfaces and is not a
  production surface.

This repository contains no credentials.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately to `contact@abstractframework.ai`, or through
GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on
[lpalbou/AbstractEntity](https://github.com/lpalbou/AbstractEntity), rather than
opening a public issue. Include a description, reproduction steps and the
affected version.

<!-- SOURCE: CONTRIBUTING.md -->
<!-- ============================================================ -->

# Contributing

AbstractEntity is a Vite + React + TypeScript app (strict TypeScript,
snake_case file names, Vitest). It is a thin client: entity state lives on
AbstractGateway, and the app renders and commands it.

## Setup

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # Vite dev server on :3007 with the gateway sign-in proxy
```

`@abstractframework/ui-kit`, `@abstractframework/panel-chat` and
`@abstractframework/app-server` are regular dependencies installed by
`npm install`. The dev server proxies `/api` to `ABSTRACTENTITY_GATEWAY_URL` (default
`http://127.0.0.1:8080`).

## Before you open a pull request

```bash
npm test         # vitest
npm run build    # tsc + vite build; must stay green
npm run check:lock  # package-lock.json matches package.json (see Lockfile check)
```

CI runs the same steps.

To check the layout at phone, tablet and desktop sizes, open the app in your
browser's device toolbar; the responsive rules are guarded by
`src/responsive_css.test.ts` and `src/side_tabs_state.test.ts`.

Voice in a visit has a browser check, `scripts/voice.e2e.mjs`: it drives the built
app (`node bin/cli.js`) against AbstractCode's isolated fixture gateway
(`abstractcode/web/e2e/gateway_fixture.py`, no model) with a fake microphone, fakes
only the speech and transcription routes, and fails on any broken step:

```bash
node scripts/voice.e2e.mjs --app http://127.0.0.1:18736 --gateway http://127.0.0.1:18737 \
  [--playwright <dir with @playwright/test>] [--shots <dir>]
```

## Avatar browser check

The optional Avatar view has a browser check over the actual built app, with
deterministic gateway route doubles and no model or external traffic:

```bash
npm run build
PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE='/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome' \
  node scripts/avatar.e2e.mjs --playwright ../abstractcode/web --shots /tmp/entity-avatar-shots
```

`--playwright` points to a project with `@playwright/test` installed. Omit the
executable override when Playwright's browser is installed. The check covers the
driver's owned reply routes and the separate summoned Flow runtime. The shared
presenter in `src/vendor/abstractchat` is generated by AbstractUIC's canonical
exporter: `npm run sync:conversation`. Never edit those artifacts directly;
the build checks their provenance hashes.

The meet console has its own browser check, run the same way:

```bash
PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE='/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome' \
  npm run e2e:meet -- --playwright ../abstractcode/web
```

It verifies the shared composer (Enter adds a line, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter relays to the
chosen speaker, the relay busy state, the empty-draft Send gate and the closing
note) on desktop and phone viewports.

## Lockfile check

`npm run check:lock` runs `scripts/check_lock.mjs`, and CI runs it before `npm ci`. It
fails when `package-lock.json` lags `package.json` (the lock's root entry records a different
dependency spec: `package.json` was edited without `npm install`), and when an
`@abstractframework/*` dependency (`ui-kit`, `panel-chat`, `app-server`, `monitor-*`) is missing
from the lock, resolves below the `package.json` floor or to another major.minor, comes from a
local `file:` tarball, or has a nested copy that differs from the top-level one. Fix it with
`npm install` (or `npm install @abstractframework/<name>@^<version>` to raise a floor) and commit
both files.

At release time, `npm run check:lock -- --latest` also fails when npm has a newer patch of an
`@abstractframework/*` dependency than the lock resolves (needs the network).

```bash
npm run check:lock
```

## Guidelines

- Keep logic in pure, tested modules (`stream_fold.ts`, `roster_empty.ts`,
  `edge_ops.ts` and similar) and keep components thin over them.
- Keep the invariants listed in [Architecture](docs/architecture.md#invariants):
  the pure fold, diary redaction, tool claims from data, and the malformed-line
  guard are pinned by tests.
- Treat [`spec/entity_phases.json`](spec/entity_phases.json) and
  [`spec/cognition_graph.json`](spec/cognition_graph.json) as shared contracts
  that the gateway and runtime also read; change them deliberately and update
  [The entity phase graph](docs/entity-phases.md) with them.
- Record user-visible changes in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and update the
  docs in the same change (see [the documentation index](docs/README.md)).
- Report security issues privately; see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
